nodes.label: Thumbnail Studio (thumbnail.py, /api/thumbnail/*)

nodes.label: burn_text: PIL Anton Text Rendering

nodes.label: Service: OpenShorts Cloud (AggregateOffer $12-$59)
nodes.rationale: Declares offerCount 4 and lowPrice 12 but lists only two offers (Free at 0 and Starter at 12).

nodes.label: NVIDIA GPU Acceleration (NVENC, CUDA)
nodes.rationale: Default image is CPU-only; the GPU build arg adds cuBLAS/cuDNN and onnxruntime-gpu (~2 GB) and the video capability is needed for NVENC. FFMPEG_ENCODER=auto probes h264_nvenc and falls back to x264; a whisper CUDA error retries once on CPU.

nodes.label: Pricing Honesty Rule (never just 'free')
nodes.rationale: Self-hosted is free and Cloud is paid; saying only 'OpenShorts is free' is what makes AI answers describe the paid product as free, so the Cloud price must be named in the same breath.

nodes.label: JSON-LD Structured Data Graph
nodes.rationale: Two products described separately on purpose: the previous single SoftwareApplication priced at 0 was true only of the self-hosted edition, so engines summarised the whole product as free.

nodes.label: Self-hosted vs Hosted Editions
nodes.rationale: Same software either way: self-hosting is free under MIT but costs a machine, own API keys and upkeep (5-8 min per 8-min video on CPU); hosted plans (free 20 min/mo watermarked, paid from $12/mo, ~50 s on NVIDIA GPU) cover hardware and keys, not feature unlocks.

nodes.label: Skill Rules (rights, confirm publishing, never 'free')
nodes.rationale: Only submit videos the user has rights to (confirm_rights is deliberate); publishing is public and irreversible so confirm platforms and caption first; download_url is valid 24h; never describe OpenShorts as simply free (self-hosted described as needing a GPU box plus own Gemini key).

nodes.label: Webhook HMAC-SHA256 Verification (n8n Code node)
nodes.rationale: The sample hashes JSON.stringify($json.body), i.e. a re-serialized object rather than the raw request bytes.

nodes.label: API Keys (osk_ tokens, cloud/api_keys.py)
nodes.rationale: sha256-stored; cloud/auth.get_current_user_optional accepts Bearer osk_ or X-API-Key, so metering, entitlement, plan priority and job ownership apply to agents with zero endpoint changes. Key management refuses API-key auth so a leaked key cannot mint replacements.

nodes.label: Completion Webhooks (webhook_url, X-OpenShorts-Signature)
nodes.rationale: Validated at submit AND at delivery to defeat DNS rebinding; fired once per job from run_job_wrapper after the R2 archive so the payload carries durable download links; PUBLIC_API_URL sets the absolute-URL base behind a proxy.

nodes.label: MCP Server (mcp_server.py, /mcp)
nodes.rationale: Stateless Streamable-HTTP JSON-RPC with no SDK dependency (~3 methods + 8 tools); each tool calls back into the same app in-process via httpx.ASGITransport forwarding the caller's auth headers, so it can never drift from REST. Cloud mode 401s without a user; self-host stays BYOK-open.

nodes.label: Resume Manifest (.resume.json heartbeat)
nodes.rationale: Running jobs heartbeat every 10 s; the resume scan re-enqueues only manifests nobody heartbeated for 60 s, so no job runs twice and none is lost; max 2 resume attempts.

nodes.label: OpenShorts CLI
nodes.rationale: Zero dependencies; talks to the same API the dashboard, MCP server and webhooks use (process, clips, publish, quota).

nodes.label: Telegram Approval Buttons
nodes.rationale: Clips over Telegram's ~20 MB URL limit fall back to a link message with the same buttons.

nodes.label: Webhook Payload (job.completed / job.failed)
nodes.rationale: Failed jobs fire the same webhook with job.failed and an error field so the flow never hangs; download_url is a 24-hour presigned link on the hosted service.

nodes.label: Built-in MCP Server (mcp.openshorts.app/mcp)
nodes.rationale: OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration for claude.ai and ChatGPT, so there is no key to copy. Lists 8 tools: process_video, create_upload, get_job_status, list_clips, get_quota, add_subtitles, recut_clip, publish_clip.

nodes.label: OpenShorts Agent Skill Package
nodes.rationale: Teaches an agent which options produce good clips, which responses look like errors but are not, and when to stop and ask; uses MCP tools when available, otherwise the REST API in reference.md. Installs unchanged in Claude Code, OpenClaw, Hermes, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor and VS Code.

nodes.label: POST /api/process
nodes.rationale: acknowledged: true is the required rights attestation; target_clips 1-15, clip_min_seconds 5-175, clip_max_seconds 10-180 and at least 5 above the minimum; errors 402 quota_exceeded, 429 too many jobs, 400 unknown duration.

nodes.label: GET /api/me (quota)
nodes.rationale: A null upload_post_profile means publishing will fail; a 404 on self-hosted simply means there is no quota.

nodes.label: POST /api/clip/rerender
nodes.rationale: Times are seconds of the original source; segments concatenate in order. Anything outside the clip's original range, or a non-auto framing (full/track), re-runs the reframe engine and needs the retained source video.

nodes.label: POST /api/social/post
nodes.rationale: Omit scheduled_date to post now; uploads are asynchronous; TikTok arrives as a draft while Instagram and YouTube publish directly.

nodes.label: Core Loop (quota, submit, webhook/poll, publish)
nodes.rationale: Check quota first for large jobs (cost is source duration rounded up, min 1 minute, same balance as the dashboard); webhooks beat polling; restyle captions before publishing if asked.

nodes.label: MCP Tools (seven listed)
nodes.rationale: Lists seven tools (process_video, get_job_status, list_clips, get_quota, add_subtitles, recut_clip, publish_clip); create_upload is not mentioned.

nodes.label: Re-cutting (recut_clip)
nodes.rationale: Segments are seconds of the original source video, not of the clip, so a recut can trim, extend, drop a dead moment or reorder; pass snap_to_words: true.

nodes.label: OpenShorts HTTP Reference
nodes.rationale: The MCP server wraps exactly these endpoints, forwarding auth headers, so the two paths cannot drift. Self-hosted needs no osk_ key but does need a Gemini key in the server env or an X-Gemini-Key header.

nodes.label: openshorts Agent Skill (v1.1.0)
nodes.rationale: One job takes minutes, so always work async: submit, then webhook or poll.

nodes.label: Prefer --webhook over --wait in Pipelines
nodes.rationale: OpenShorts POSTs once (HMAC-signed X-OpenShorts-Signature) when the job ends, with clip titles and durable download links, instead of a blocking wait.

nodes.label: Content Machine Workflow (openshorts-content-machine.json)
nodes.rationale: One video a day from the channel RSS keeps quota burn predictable; a 402 pauses the machine and alerts on Telegram instead of failing silently. Processed-video memory lives in n8n workflow static data, which persists only for production executions.

nodes.label: Drip-publish Scheduling
nodes.rationale: Each approved clip takes the next free daily slot read from the queue the server holds (GET /api/social/scheduled), deliberately not workflow static data, so two clips approved seconds apart cannot book the same slot.

nodes.label: Webhook Delivery and Raw-body HMAC Verification
nodes.norm_label: webhook delivery and raw-body hmac verification
nodes.rationale: Fired once on success and failure so a flow never hangs; the URL must be public HTTPS, validated at submit and re-resolved at delivery; the HMAC-SHA256 signature must be verified against the raw request bytes, not a re-serialized object.

nodes.label: YOUTUBE_COOKIES Codespaces Secret
nodes.rationale: YouTube blocks downloads from cloud servers ('Sign in to confirm you're not a bot'), so uploading the file is safest. Netscape cookies.txt grants account access: never paste it in chat or the repo, and prefer a secondary account since YouTube may restrict accounts used to download.

nodes.label: Coolify Rolling Update
nodes.rationale: Every push to main redeploys (~5 min build plus handover), so small commits should be batched with the next real change.

nodes.label: Core Processing Pipeline (11 steps)
nodes.rationale: Ingest (yt-dlp/upload), transcription, scene detection, Gemini analysis of 3-15 moments, FFmpeg extraction, AI cropping, effects/subtitles, hook overlay, optional dubbing, silent S3 backup, Upload-Post distribution.

nodes.label: .transcript_checkpoint.json
nodes.rationale: Left in the job dir so a re-run job skips the paid transcription.

nodes.label: Core Python Dependencies
nodes.rationale: All pinned except yt-dlp, which floats (likely to keep up with YouTube changes).

nodes.label: Deploy Handover and Drain
nodes.rationale: Both containers share output/, so the instance that sees another id in output/.instance drains (finishes running jobs, starts none). SIGTERM drains up to DRAIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 840 (below the 900 s Coolify grace), keeps serving PROXY_DRAIN_SECONDS 20 so Traefik notices, then HARD_EXIT_SECONDS 30 because a hung executor thread kept the interpreter alive; uvicorn --timeout-graceful-shutdown 15 caps open connections.

nodes.label: /health/ready Readiness Probe
nodes.rationale: Traefik's docker provider only routes to healthy containers, so an instance answers 503 from SIGTERM; Coolify replaces the Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK with its own curl/wget (5 s x 3), so the image must ship curl or every deploy rolls back. /health stays a plain liveness probe.

nodes.label: React Compiler (not enabled)
nodes.rationale: Not enabled because of its impact on dev and build performance.

nodes.label: Three Non-failure Responses (needs_confirmation, 402, 429)
nodes.rationale: needs_confirmation (HTTP 200): ask the user, never auto-retry with force_low_quality because it still costs minutes. 402 quota_exceeded: report and stop, never split the video to squeeze under the limit. 429: wait for a running job instead of resubmitting.

nodes.label: Codespaces Free Account Limits
nodes.rationale: 120 core-hours/month on a 2-core codespace is about 60 hours; 15 GB storage (videos live in uploads/ and output/); idle shutdown after 30 min should be raised (up to 240) so long processing is not cut; stop the codespace when done because it burns hours while running.

nodes.rationale: With a Gemini key a professional AI watches the best moments, picks cuts, adjusts in/out points, writes Portuguese title, description, hashtags and hook, and fixes wrong subtitle words. Frames and speech of candidate moments are sent to Google; free quota may be exceeded and billed.

nodes.label: Security & Performance
nodes.rationale: Non-root appuser, semaphore job queue, 1h auto-cleanup, client-side encrypted API keys never stored server-side, image upload validation, 2 GB upload limit.

nodes.label: SEO / AI-crawler Surface
nodes.rationale: The dashboard is a hash-routed SPA whose served HTML had an empty #root; Googlebot renders JS but GPTBot, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot do not and measured the homepage as zero characters, so crawler-visible content is injected at build time.

nodes.label: Canonical URL (www.openshorts.app)
nodes.rationale: The apex redirects to www, so a canonical pointing at the apex named a URL that only ever redirects.

nodes.label: robots.txt Crawler Policy
nodes.rationale: Search and AI crawlers are all welcome; the AI crawlers do not execute JavaScript, so they read the static HTML shipped by the build (injected homepage content and standalone pages under /alternatives), never the hydrated app.

nodes.label: Single Brass Accent (coral verb-landmark only)
nodes.rationale: Tools are differentiated by mono eyebrow ordinals (01 CLIPS, 02 AI SHORTS), not hue; the old per-tab violet/emerald/amber/teal coding is retired.

nodes.label: Functional Contract (never break)
nodes.rationale: Redesign is classes and markup only: hash routing anchors, billingEnabled/isManaged/isSignedIn gating, handlers and props, localStorage keys (gemini_key, uploadPostKey_v3, elevenLabsKey_v1, falKey_v1, openshorts_session, ...), API calls and BYOK headers, QuotaError flows and Remotion preview/render wiring.

nodes.label: Hard Bans (Lumen)
nodes.rationale: No italics, gradients, backdrop-blur, glowing orbs, invented metrics, emoji icons in chrome, rounded-2xl soup, hardcoded colors or Title Case UI copy.

nodes.label: Lumen Night Foundry Design System
nodes.rationale: A locked system read before every page redesign and extended rather than regenerated per page; premium AI-tool register where the product's own numbers (timecodes, ratios, clip counts, costs) are the decoration as UPPERCASE mono readouts.

nodes.label: Two-register Typography (lowercase prose / UPPERCASE mono)
nodes.rationale: Instrument Serif display, Geist body, JetBrains Mono labels; the lowercase/UPPERCASE contrast is the typographic signature. Never lowercase user content (titles, captions, API keys, logs), so the class is applied per element with no global text-transform.

nodes.label: ALTERNATE Mode (active_speaker.py)
nodes.rationale: Hard cuts to whoever is talking via the TRACK path. Mouth activity must be normalised per speaker (normalise_activity) because raw frame-difference scales with contrast and lighting and handed one speaker 90-100% of a real two-shot.

nodes.label: Captions on the Seam (subtitles.generate_ass)
nodes.rationale: On SPLIT stretches captions sit on the seam between the halves, the one place they cover nobody; only the ASS path can do this, SRT burns keep one alignment for the whole file.

nodes.label: INSET Mode (camera_inset.py)
nodes.rationale: Chained behind the screencast decision rather than asked of Gemini: offered as a fourth option Gemini answered screencast on all 5 inset clips and accuracy fell from 92% to 83-85%. The geometric detector (small, horizontally off-centre, still between samples) finds all 5 with no false positives.

nodes.label: Layout Picker (layout_picker.py)
nodes.rationale: One Gemini call per source video (not per clip) choosing none/screencast/split; 94%/92%/96% over three passes on a 48-clip hand-labelled corpus with 0-1 false positives. apply() only adds: an explicit user choice is never disabled because the model says none.

nodes.label: layout_ranges Sidecar (<clip>.layout.json)
nodes.rationale: Records which stretches are stacked; every metadata writer copies it into the clip's layout_ranges so /api/subtitle finds it after a restyle; layout_ranges.remap carries ranges through recut.perform_recut on fast rerender.

nodes.label: Per-job Layout Selection (layouts param)
nodes.rationale: POST /api/process layouts (auto, split, screencast, speaker_cut, punch_in, none) turns on each env var for that job only (app.py:layout_env); none disables the picker even with AUTO_LAYOUT=1, the deployment default since 25-Aug-2026. Exposed in MediaInput.jsx, remembered in localStorage.os_layout.

nodes.label: Punch-in (punch_in.py)
nodes.rationale: Not a layout: a ~12% push on beats riding the TRACK path by widening its per-frame crop from x-only to w/h/x/y; emphasis_times is a plain list of seconds so transcript hook words can replace the audio envelope later.

nodes.label: SCREENCAST / WIDE Modes (screencast_layout.py)
nodes.rationale: Gemini-reported width_fraction is the gate (coverage did not separate a spreadsheet from a corner ticker, width does): below 0.5 nothing moves, 0.5-0.85 stacks content over the presenter, above 0.85 the presenter is composited on top so WIDE (GENERAL without side-cropping) is used.

nodes.label: SPLIT Mode (split_layout.py)
nodes.rationale: Needs both faces visible in the same frame for at least half the sampled frames, which separates a real two-shot from shot/reverse-shot where stacking would show the same person twice. Off by default (SPLIT_LAYOUT=1), v2 engine only (v1 fallback silently renders GENERAL), upgrades only GENERAL scenes; SPLIT_TIGHTNESS 0.8.

nodes.label: TRACK Mode (single subject)
nodes.rationale: MediaPipe face detection with YOLOv8 fallback and 'Heavy Tripod' stabilization.

nodes.label: FAQPage Structured Data
nodes.rationale: Answers what OpenShorts is, pricing per edition, moment detection, cropping (described as two modes, TRACK and GENERAL), Opus Clip alternative, subtitles/dubbing and open-source status.

nodes.label: OpenShorts vs Competitors (Opus Clip, CapCut, Vizard, Klap, Descript)
nodes.norm_label: openshorts vs competitors (opus clip, capcut, vizard, klap, descript)

nodes.label: Closed-choice Decision over Continuous Measurement
nodes.rationale: Four earlier attempts (Canny, MSER, temporal coverage, width) asked the model for a number and none separated a spreadsheet from a corner ticker; the variance blamed on Gemini came from continuous measures, not the model.

nodes.label: Send Frames, Not Video, to Gemini
nodes.norm_label: send frames, not video, to gemini
nodes.rationale: Gemini bills video at ~300 tokens/s (an hour is ~1.08M tokens, more than a 1M window, plus a 1-2 GB upload); 12 frames at 1024px cost ~3k tokens whatever the source length. Resolution matters and frame count does not (640px finds 15/20, 1024px 17/20, 24 frames is worse); 2.2 s per clip instead of ~15 s.

nodes.label: Choices the API Cannot Make (target_clips, length, aspect, layouts)
nodes.norm_label: choices the api cannot make (target_clips, length, aspect, layouts)
nodes.rationale: Leave target_clips unset (most videos yield 2-6; asking a short video for 15 adds filler); keep the 15-60 s defaults platforms reward; output_format is an aspect not a resolution; leave layouts empty or ['auto'], since split is wrong for shot/reverse-shot and punch_in composes with the others.

nodes.label: OAuth for MCP Clients (cloud/mcp_oauth.py)
nodes.rationale: RFC 9728/8414 metadata, dynamic client registration, PKCE S256 mandatory; /oauth/authorize bounces to the dashboard consent screen because the session JWT lives in frontend localStorage. /oauth/token mints an ordinary osk_ key: no new auth path, no refresh tokens, revoking the key disconnects the app. oauth_clients deliberately not in USER_OWNED_TABLES.

nodes.label: USER_OWNED_TABLES
nodes.rationale: tests/test_account_erasure.py fails if a new table references users.id without joining this list.

nodes.label: Disposable Email Domain Blocklist
nodes.rationale: Blocks temp-mail domains from sign-up: a strong curated subset of the upstream list plus every abusive domain seen in own sign-ups; add new ones as they appear. Note: 33mail.com is listed twice.

nodes.label: Account Erasure (DELETE /api/account, GDPR art. 17)
nodes.rationale: Immediate and irreversible; refuses API-key auth and requires retyping the email. Step order is the design: Stripe cancel first (abort on failure, never erase a billed user), R2 before the DB (rows are the only index of objects), DB delete in one transaction over an explicit table list because create_all never ALTERs existing tables. Stripe invoices kept 6 years (Spanish law); a sha256-of-email proof row kept 5 years. _apply_topup now checks the user row exists to avoid 3 days of Stripe retries.
